behaviour: Turns a missed entity ref into a same-origin redirect and its navigation state, or undefined, and never rejects.
rules: 1. Wrap the whole body in try/catch; any error returns undefined, so a resolver failure leaves the caller's not-found state untouched.
2. `const currentRef = await options.catalogApi.resolveFormerEntityRef?.(options.entityRef);`. Return undefined when it is falsy.
3. `const root = options.routeFunc(options.entityRef);`. The sub-path is `location.pathname.slice(root.length)` when `location.pathname` starts with `root`, else empty.

4. `to` is `options.routeFunc(entityRouteParams(currentRef))` + sub-path + `location.search` + `location.hash`. Build it only from the route function and the current location; never navigate to a value from an annotation or a response other than through the route function.
5. `state.entityRenamedFrom` is `namespace/name` of `options.entityRef`, or just `name` when the namespace equals `DEFAULT_NAMESPACE` compared lower-cased.

behaviour: Shows a dismissible notice from in-app navigation state, and nothing otherwise.
rules: 1. `EntityRenamedNotice` reads `useLocation()` and takes `formerName` from `location.state?.entityRenamedFrom`. If that is not a string it returns null, before any translation hook runs: an inner component holds the `useTranslationRef` call, so a page with no state pays nothing.
2. Read nothing from the URL, so a crafted link cannot make a page claim a rename.
3. Dismissal is `useState` holding the `location.key` that was dismissed; the notice is hidden while that key is current.

4. Render `Alert` from `@backstage/ui` with `status="info"`, `icon`, `mb="4"`, `title={t('entityRenamedNotice.title', { formerName })}`, and `customActions` holding a `Button` with `size="small"`, `variant="tertiary"` and `t('entityRenamedNotice.dismiss')` that dismisses on press.
5. Use `catalogReactTranslationRef` from `../../translation` and `useTranslationRef` from `@backstage/core-plugin-api/alpha`.

behaviour: After a miss, and only then, asks the resolver within the same async load and redirects with history replace, for both frontend systems.
rules: 1. Also use `useLocation` from `react-router-dom`, `useRouteRef` from `@backstage/core-plugin-api` as `entityRoute = useRouteRef(entityRouteRef)`, and `resolveEntityRename` from `@backstage/plugin-catalog-react`.
2. Compute `routeKey = `${kind}:${namespace}/${name}``.

3. The `useAsyncRetry` function, with the same deps `[catalogApi, kind, namespace, name]`, awaits `catalogApi.getEntityByRef({ kind, namespace, name })` and returns `{ entity }` when found. Only otherwise it awaits `resolveEntityRename({ catalogApi, entityRef: { kind, namespace, name }, location, routeFunc: entityRoute })` and returns `{ redirect, routeKey }`. A rejection of `getEntityByRef` stays an `error`, with no resolver call.

4. A `useEffect` calls `navigate(redirect.to, { replace: true, state: redirect.state })` only when `value?.redirect` is set and `value.routeKey === routeKey`, so a stale result cannot navigate again after the route params change.
5. Keep the existing `!name` effect unchanged.
6. Return `{ entity: value?.entity, loading: loading || !!value?.redirect, error, refresh }`: `loading` holds across both calls and until the route has changed, so the page never flashes not-found.

rules: 1. The async value becomes `{ from: string; to: string; state?: EntityRenamedLocationState } | undefined`, where `from` is `entityKey`.
